title: Void Ending in a Square to Mars
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The square is one of the two worst aspects in the lunar doctrine, an enmity the text grades as moderate because the signs it joins stand two natures apart. The counsel that guards every election runs exactly here: watch the square and the opposition in everything, and keep the Moon from the unfortunate planets in these figures above all.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a square to Mars, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his fire and his knife. Mars is the planet of the knife and the forge: surgery, bloodletting, the taming of wild beasts, the smithy's fire, war, and banditry fall under him, with army camps, battlefields, and places of judgment among his locations. His seat in the body is the gallbladder, the source of yellow bile and heat, and bright red is his color. A waxing Moon facing him by aspect is counted a misfortune; his is the figure the lunar doctrine watches hardest.
